contradicted: The mission's step 3 ('Bound the bare search... scope it by the viewport county when the client knows one, and when it does not, return a declared refusal') implicitly framed the ~5s live timeout as a slow, unscoped STATEWIDE SCAN problem. EXPLAIN (planning only, no execution) on both the equality street-key query and the ILIKE prefix fallback, each bound across all 254 Texas county FIPS codes, showed efficient Index Scans on txgio_parcel_situs_norm_idx with LOW estimated cost (~1500 units) in both cases -- not a slow scan by the query planner's own accounting. The real, measured mechanism was a caller/callee budget mismatch: this route's own SITUS_SEARCH_BUDGET_MS was 20,000ms while hauska-map's PE proxy (api/pe-situs-search.ts) aborts its own fetch at a hardcoded UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS = 5,000ms -- four times shorter. A bare query needing the full situs/prefix/address-point ladder raced past the caller's patience and came back as an unlabelled 502 before this route's own honest SITUS_SEARCH_BUDGET_ERROR response ever had a chance to fire. Fixed with a tighter 4,000ms budget specifically for the no-locality-parsed case (comfortably inside the proxy's 5,000ms window), not by scoping the query to a client-supplied viewport county -- I did not implement viewport-county scoping (named as a deferred item below); the budget-tiering fix addresses the measured symptom directly without requiring new client-to-server plumbing.

Neither the dispatch nor my own CP1 anticipated the CI ci-vintage-predicate guard, which caught a real correctness defect in the first cut of migration 0100 (picking the CAD row by max(tax_year) rather than the county's declared vintage) before it ever reached staging re-validation, let alone production. This is recorded here per DEV_PROCESS's instrument-traceability rule, not as a complaint about the guard -- the guard did exactly its job.

texasCountyFipsList() (txgioAddressNormalize.ts) returns literally all 254 Texas county FIPS codes, not the subset of counties actually loaded into txgio_parcel/txgio_address. This is real, pre-existing over-coverage in every situs-search query (not something this lane introduced or fixed) -- every search probes all 254 county partitions of the index regardless of relevance. It did not turn out to be the dominant cost (see the EXPLAIN finding above), so this lane did not touch it, but it is a real inefficiency worth a future lane's attention: a corrected 'counties actually in the store' registry (recall allStoreCounties() already exists but under-covers, missing Bastrop) would need to be derived and kept honestly in sync, not guessed.

P-27 is the situs-index-over-geocoder ruling this supersedes any drift from.
